The measurements of the original are given in Table 2 (dealate alates) and Table 3 (soldiers), and those two tables are not provided with the treatment page, so this entry cites only the values given in the key and the text (left mandible length 0.57 mm) and does not invent the remaining measurements. The type soldier comes from Laguna Guaimoreto, Cortés Department, Honduras (16.0132°N, 85.9184°W, altitude 6 m), collected on 29 May 2007 by J. A. Chase and deposited in the University of Florida termite collection (UF no. HN273); the specific name refers to the Garifuna people of the Honduran coast.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In lateral view the head grades from transparent at the neck margin to dark rusty brown at the frontal margin; in dorsal view it is mottled reddish brown to dark rusty brown, in keeping with the thickness of the cuticular rugosity. Mandibles concolorous with the frons. Anterior margin of the pronotum yellowish brown, the rest yellow. Head capsule in dorsal view cubic, the sides almost parallel until the frontal margin projects forwards; head capsule in lateral view with the dorsal margin weakly S-shaped from the frontal margin to the occiput. Dorsal rugosity moderate, coarser in the anterior half (including the frontal margin and the frons). Frons deeply concave. Frontal margin stout and raised, its median notch connected with the median depression of the vertex; in dorsal view the frontal margin forms an arc of 120°. Eye spots very faint. Labrum short, upturned at the apex. Mandibles short, angular, curved about 120°, finely rugose, with weak dentition.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: In dorsal view the frontal horns are large and globular, projecting beyond the frontal margin and reaching the posterior margin of the postclypeus; the genal horns are small and blunt, their apices level with the anterior margin of the antennal socket. In lateral view the frontal horns are nearly semicircular, projecting beyond the base of the genal horns. Antenna 11-segmented, the segment formula 2>3=4<5. Anterior margin of the pronotum with weak, irregular undulating notches, the anterolateral corners nearly square, the lateral and posterior margins forming an evenly rounded outline. Left mandible length 0.57 mm (value from the key).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dealate male: head and tergites pale yellowish brown. Postclypeus transparent. The chevron mark on the forewing scale slightly darker than the mesonotum. Legs very pale yellow, concolorous with the sternites. Compound eyes dark grey, occupying 2/5 of the distance from the vertex to the genal margin, oval, with the margin straight at the antennal socket. Ocelli medium-sized, transparent, touching the compound eye, oval, with a fine pointed papilla on the dorsal margin. Antennal segment formula 2>3<4<5. Pronotum wider than long, distinctly narrower than the head width at the compound eyes; anterior and posterior margins nearly straight, the sides slightly convex. Tarsal arolia present.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Among New World Cryptotermes the dealate alates of this species, C. fatulus and C. undulans are the smallest, and this species is paler yellow than the other two. The soldier is one of the smallest in the New World, with only C. fatulus of similar size, but in the latter the head capsule is not rugose. In the key of Scheffrahn & Křeček (1999) the species runs to couplet 10 and is close to C. darlingtonae, from which it differs in: genal horns blunt, their apices level with the anterior margin of the antennal socket (in darlingtonae the genal horns project forwards and stand only slightly behind the frontal horns), left mandible length 0.57 mm (0.68—0.75 mm in darlingtonae).
